input: Freeze a month's worth of baby food portions

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The types of food (purees, soft chunks, finger foods, single-ingredient vs. mixed) completely change what needs to be cooked, blended, and stored — and how many different batches to prepare.
The baby's age and stage determines texture, portion size, and which ingredients are safe; knowing who is doing the cooking affects how much help or equipment is assumed.
Available freezer space and type (chest freezer vs. fridge-top) dictates how many portions can realistically be stored and in what containers.
A budget limit affects whether to buy fresh, organic, or frozen produce in bulk, and how many cooking sessions are feasible.
The portioning tool — ice cube trays, silicone molds, small jars — affects the batch workflow, labeling system, and how food is thawed and served.
Dietary preferences or restrictions (vegetarian, allergies already identified, foods the baby has already tried) shape which recipes and ingredients to include or exclude.

Knowing what 'done well' looks like — e.g., a set number of daily servings covered, full nutritional variety, or a specific number of freezer bags ready — determines when the task is actually complete.

gold.taskTitle: Freeze a month of baby food portions
gold.taskDescription: Prepare, portion, and freeze approximately one month's supply of baby food in a way that suits the baby's age, dietary needs, and the caregiver's kitchen setup.

questions.title: What foods or food groups should be included?
questions.description: Identify which fruits, vegetables, proteins, or grains to prepare — and whether these are single-ingredient purees, mixed meals, or textured soft foods.

questions.title: How old is the baby, and what texture stage are they at?
questions.description: Determine the baby's age and feeding stage to set the right consistency, portion size, and safe ingredient list.

questions.title: How much freezer space is available for this batch?
questions.description: Assess the type and capacity of the freezer to plan realistically how many portions can be stored at once.

questions.title: What is the budget for ingredients and supplies?
questions.description: Set a spending limit to decide whether to buy fresh, organic, or bulk frozen produce, and whether new storage tools are needed.

questions.title: What containers or molds will you use for portioning?
questions.description: Decide on the storage format — silicone trays, small pouches, jars — which shapes the entire batch prep and labeling workflow.

questions.title: Are there any ingredients to avoid or dietary rules to follow?
questions.description: Note any allergens already identified, foods not yet introduced, or family dietary preferences that restrict what goes into the freezer batches.

questions.title: How many daily servings should this batch fully cover?
questions.description: Define what a complete month's supply means — total number of portions, meals per day, or specific variety targets — so there is a clear finish line.
